variants.as_reported: three missense mutations resulting in the substitution of conserved amino acids

quotes: Mutations in the complex I NDUFS2 gene of patients with cardiomyopathy and encephalomyopathy.

Screening of patient NDUFS2 cDNA by reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) in combination with direct DNA sequencing revealed three missense mutations resulting in the substitution of conserved amino acids in three families.

records.label: Three affected sibs of a consanguineous family

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

quotes: a 4-bp deletion in intron 2 (IVS2+5_+8delGTAA) of the NDUFV2 gene (encoding NADH dehydrogenase ubiquinone flavoprotein 2) causes complex I deficiency and early onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with trunk hypotonia in three affected sibs of a consanguineous family.
The homozygous mutation altering the consensus splice-donor site of exon 2 resulted in 70% decreased NDUFV2 protein and complex I deficiency.

records.label: Family 1 (two siblings)

phenotypes.text: low complex I activity in muscle
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

quotes: Two siblings with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and brain atrophy were diagnosed with Complex I deficiency based on low enzyme activity in muscle and high lactate/pyruvate ratio in fibroblasts.
Two compound heterozygous mutations were identified in both siblings in NDUFV2, encoding the 24 kDa subunit of Complex I.
The other mutation is novel (c.669_670insG, p.Ser224Valfs*3) and predicted to cause a pathogenic frameshift in the protein.

records.label: Family 2 (consanguineous, three affected siblings)

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

quotes: revealed homozygosity for the intronic c.IVS2 + 1delGTAA mutation in a second, consanguineous family. In this family three of five siblings were affected. Interestingly, they presented with Leigh syndrome but no cardiac involvement.

notes.statement: Cameron et al. (2015) noted that homozygosity for the NDUFV2 c.IVS2+1delGTAA mutation, previously reported in 2 families with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, trunk hypotonia, and encephalopathy, caused Leigh syndrome without cardiac involvement in their consanguineous family, expanding the phenotypic spectrum associated with this mutation.
quotes: The same genotype had been reported previously in a two families but presenting with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, trunk hypotonia and encephalopathy.
The diagnosis of Leigh syndrome expands the clinical phenotypes associated with the c.IVS2 + 1delGTAA mutation in this gene.

notes.statement: Cameron et al. (2015) identified the NDUFV2 mutations by whole-exome sequencing of fibroblast DNA from one sib, filtered to 190 novel nonsynonymous variants in 185 candidate genes, and then screened 10 probands with complex I deficiency from different families, finding a second family.
quotes: Whole exome sequencing results of fibroblast gDNA from one sibling was narrowed down to 190 SNPs or In/Dels in 185 candidate genes by selecting non-synonymous coding sequence base pair changes that were not present in the SNP database.
Subsequent investigation of 10 probands with complex I deficiency from different families revealed homozygosity

notes.statement: Pagniez-Mammeri et al. (2009) screened 8 patients with biochemically proven isolated complex I deficiency for mutations in 8 nuclear complex I genes (NDUFS1, NDUFS2, NDUFS3, NDUFS4, NDUFS7, NDUFS8, NDUFV1, and NDUFV2). They used Surveyor nuclease digestion of 22 cDNA fragments and found molecular defects in 3 patients. They concluded that the method was a reliable way to genotype nuclear complex I deficiencies and would enhance the possibility of prenatal diagnosis.
quotes: Eight complex I nuclear genes, among the most frequently mutated (NDUFS1, NDUFS2, NDUFS3, NDUFS4, NDUFS7, NDUFS8, NDUFV1 and NDUFV2), were studied in 22 cDNA fragments spanning their coding sequences in 8 patients with a biochemically proved complex I deficiency.
Molecular defects were detected in 3 patients.
Surveyor nuclease screening is a reliable method for genotyping nuclear complex I deficiencies, easy to interpret, and limits the number of sequence reactions.

notes.statement: Bénit et al. (2003) found that the homozygous NDUFV2 IVS2+5_+8delGTAA mutation, which altered the consensus splice-donor site of exon 2, resulted in a 70% decrease in NDUFV2 protein and complex I deficiency.
quotes: The homozygous mutation altering the consensus splice-donor site of exon 2 resulted in 70% decreased NDUFV2 protein and complex I deficiency.

notes.statement: Bénit et al. (2003) noted that mutations in many complex I subunit genes mainly cause neurologic symptoms, whereas this first NDUFV2 mutation was strikingly associated with cardiomyopathy, as seen before only in the unique case of NDUFS2 mutations.
quotes: While mutation in a number of genes encoding complex I subunits essentially result in neurological symptoms, this first mutation in NDUFV2 is strikingly associated with cardiomyopathy, as previously observed in the unique case of NDFUS2 mutations.

notes.statement: Loeffen et al. (2001) noted a high rate of consanguinity and an autosomal recessive pattern of inheritance in their group of patients with complex I deficiency. Because common mtDNA mutations were also absent, they considered a nuclear genetic cause likely.
quotes: a high percentage of consanguinity and an autosomal-recessive mode of inheritance observed within our patient group as well as the absence of common mtDNA mutations make a nuclear genetic cause likely

notes.statement: Loeffen et al. (2001) chose NDUFS2 as a candidate gene because its protein is part of complex I in many prokaryotes and eukaryotes. They used RT-PCR and direct sequencing to screen NDUFS2 cDNA from patients with enzymatic complex I deficiency, and found 3 missense mutations that changed conserved amino acids in 3 families.
quotes: The NDUFS2 protein is part of complex I of many pro- and eukaryotes. The nuclear gene coding for this protein is therefore an important candidate for mutational detection studies in enzymatic complex I deficient patients.
